beginner.problemText:
A study of venomous snakebites in the US has shown that most of the people bitten were deliberately interacting with snakes, and 90% of those people were men. Suppose that 3 people are bitten by venomous snakes. The bites are independent of each other.

Let X be the number of men among the 3 people bitten. Use the probability table below.

| X (number of men) | P(X) |
|---:|---:|
| 0 | 0.001 |
| 1 | 0.027 |
| 2 | 0.243 |
| 3 | 0.729 |

Compute the expected value of X. Then explain what the expected value means as a long-run average in this situation. Do not interpret it as the number of men in every single group of 3 people.
linguisticNotes: Uses short sentences and familiar vocabulary.
Defines X in plain language.
Explicitly connects the interpretation to a long-run average.

The rules state participants must look “fantastic.” Let X represent the number of items dropped by a randomly selected competitor during the race. The probability distribution of X is shown below.

| x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P(X = x) | 0.10 | 0.15 | 0.30 | 0.45 |

Find the variance and standard deviation of X. Express the standard deviation in items dropped.
